title: Deterministic workflows vs agentic systems
core_idea: Use deterministic workflows when steps and decision rules are known; use agentic behaviour when the system must dynamically choose actions.
architect_note: Autonomy adds flexibility but also latency, non-determinism and failure surfaces. Use the simplest architecture that meets requirements.
explanation: Autonomy adds flexibility but also latency, non-determinism and failure surfaces. Use the simplest architecture that meets requirements.

title: Orchestration and specialist agents
core_idea: An orchestrator coordinates tasks, context and control flow among specialist components.
architect_note: Use multiple agents only when separation of responsibilities or parallelism justifies coordination overhead.
explanation: Use multiple agents only when separation of responsibilities or parallelism justifies coordination overhead.

title: Architecture trade-offs
core_idea: Architecture selects a design that satisfies requirements under constraints; there is rarely one universally best solution.
architect_note: Compare latency, reliability, security, cost, maintainability, scalability and observability.
explanation: Compare latency, reliability, security, cost, maintainability, scalability and observability.

title: Human-in-the-loop design
core_idea: Human review is useful for high-impact, ambiguous or irreversible decisions.
architect_note: Define escalation thresholds, reviewer context, approval actions and audit trails.
explanation: Define escalation thresholds, reviewer context, approval actions and audit trails.

title: Reliability and graceful degradation
core_idea: Design systems to remain safe and useful when a model, tool, network or dependency fails.
architect_note: Use bounded retries, timeouts, fallbacks, idempotency and clear failure states.
explanation: Use bounded retries, timeouts, fallbacks, idempotency and clear failure states.

title: System instructions and prompt hierarchy
core_idea: System instructions establish role, boundaries and operating rules.
architect_note: Prompts are guidance, not a security boundary; enforce permissions and validation in application code.
explanation: Prompts are guidance, not a security boundary; enforce permissions and validation in application code.

title: Context engineering
core_idea: Context engineering selects, organises and maintains information supplied to a model.
architect_note: Prioritise relevant, current, authoritative context; manage token budgets and provenance.
explanation: Prioritise relevant, current, authoritative context; manage token budgets and provenance.

title: Prompt chaining
core_idea: Prompt chaining decomposes a complex task into sequential model calls.
architect_note: Use intermediate schemas and validation; extra calls add latency and possible error propagation.
explanation: Use intermediate schemas and validation; extra calls add latency and possible error propagation.

title: Structured output and JSON schemas
core_idea: Structured output constrains response format; tool schemas define tool argument structure.
architect_note: Validate syntax and semantic correctness at the application boundary.
explanation: Validate syntax and semantic correctness at the application boundary.

title: Model selection and effort settings
core_idea: Choose model and reasoning effort based on measured performance, latency, cost and reliability.
architect_note: Benchmark representative tasks and verify current API configuration before deployment.
explanation: Benchmark representative tasks and verify current API configuration before deployment.

title: Prompt injection and untrusted context
core_idea: Untrusted input may attempt to redirect model behaviour or misuse tools.
architect_note: Use least-privilege tools, server-side authorisation, data separation and confirmation for consequential actions.
explanation: Use least-privilege tools, server-side authorisation, data separation and confirmation for consequential actions.

title: Tool use lifecycle
core_idea: A tool-enabled assistant selects a tool, provides arguments, receives results and continues.
architect_note: Validate arguments, enforce permissions outside the model, set timeouts and log tool calls.
explanation: Validate arguments, enforce permissions outside the model, set timeouts and log tool calls.

title: MCP concepts
core_idea: MCP standardises how AI applications connect to external tools and context providers.
architect_note: Review server trust, authentication, permissions, data exposure and version compatibility.
explanation: Review server trust, authentication, permissions, data exposure and version compatibility.

title: API integration and error handling
core_idea: Reliable integrations handle authentication, validation, rate limits, timeouts, retries and partial failure.
architect_note: Use backoff and idempotency carefully; do not blindly retry non-idempotent actions.
explanation: Use backoff and idempotency carefully; do not blindly retry non-idempotent actions.

title: Retrieval-augmented generation
core_idea: RAG retrieves external information and supplies it to a model to ground responses.
architect_note: Evaluate chunking, metadata, hybrid retrieval, reranking, freshness, citations and access filters.
explanation: Evaluate chunking, metadata, hybrid retrieval, reranking, freshness, citations and access filters.

title: Evaluation datasets
core_idea: Evaluation datasets contain representative inputs and expected outcomes or grading criteria.
architect_note: Maintain common, edge and adversarial cases; version and refresh datasets.
explanation: Maintain common, edge and adversarial cases; version and refresh datasets.

title: LLM-as-judge
core_idea: An LLM judge scores outputs against a rubric but can show inconsistency and preference bias.
architect_note: Calibrate against human labels and audit periodically; judge rationales do not prove correctness.
explanation: Calibrate against human labels and audit periodically; judge rationales do not prove correctness.

title: Observability and distributed tracing
core_idea: Traces, metrics and logs explain system behaviour across model calls, tools and services.
architect_note: Track latency, errors, token usage and tool outcomes while protecting sensitive data.
explanation: Track latency, errors, token usage and tool outcomes while protecting sensitive data.

title: Regression testing and release gates
core_idea: Regression tests check that changes do not break acceptable behaviour.
architect_note: Run representative evaluations after model, prompt, tool, retrieval or code changes.
explanation: Run representative evaluations after model, prompt, tool, retrieval or code changes.

title: Optimisation and caching
core_idea: Caching can reduce repeated computation when requests or context are reusable.
architect_note: Measure hit rates, freshness, invalidation and privacy; savings are workload-dependent.
explanation: Measure hit rates, freshness, invalidation and privacy; savings are workload-dependent.

title: Layered safety controls
core_idea: Safety is enforced through model instructions, application validation, tool permissions, monitoring and human escalation.
architect_note: Assume any one layer can fail; prompts and hooks are not universal security boundaries.
explanation: Assume any one layer can fail; prompts and hooks are not universal security boundaries.

title: Data privacy and minimisation
core_idea: Collect and expose only data needed for the task.
architect_note: Define retention, access control, encryption, redaction and deletion processes.
explanation: Define retention, access control, encryption, redaction and deletion processes.

title: Governance and auditability
core_idea: Governance establishes accountability, ownership, acceptable use and evidence of controls.
architect_note: Maintain inventories, risk assessments, change records, incident procedures and named owners.
explanation: Maintain inventories, risk assessments, change records, incident procedures and named owners.

title: Secure tool permissions
core_idea: Tools should expose only the minimum actions and data needed.
architect_note: Separate read/write permissions, scope credentials and require confirmation for consequential actions.
explanation: Separate read/write permissions, scope credentials and require confirmation for consequential actions.

title: Requirements discovery
core_idea: Architecture begins by identifying users, tasks, constraints, success measures and risks.
architect_note: Convert broad requests into testable functional and non-functional requirements.
explanation: Convert broad requests into testable functional and non-functional requirements.

title: Stakeholder communication
core_idea: Communicate decisions in terms of outcomes, constraints, trade-offs and evidence.
architect_note: Record assumptions, risks, owners and next steps in concise decision records.
explanation: Record assumptions, risks, owners and next steps in concise decision records.

title: Lifecycle and change management
core_idea: AI systems require ownership across design, testing, deployment, monitoring and retirement.
architect_note: Define release ownership, versioning, change approval, rollback and incident response.
explanation: Define release ownership, versioning, change approval, rollback and incident response.

title: Developer productivity and reusable patterns
core_idea: Reusable templates, typed interfaces and test fixtures reduce repeated effort.
architect_note: Keep examples current and review generated code; measure safe delivery, not code volume.
explanation: Keep examples current and review generated code; measure safe delivery, not code volume.

title: Hooks and controlled extension points
core_idea: Hooks provide defined points to observe or influence application lifecycle events.
architect_note: Hooks complement security controls; validate actions in trusted runtime and test bypass paths.
explanation: Hooks complement security controls; validate actions in trusted runtime and test bypass paths.
